how: Claude agent reading of the stored title + abstract, blind to the curated graph, with EXTRACT_INSTRUCTIONS and CLAIM_SCHEMA

claims.quote: Severe gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms occur in people with CLN3 disease, a neurodegenerative disorder.
Human CLN3 bowel displayed a profound loss of enteric neurons and their neurites, with pathological effects upon enteric glia.

claims.object_mention: neurodegeneration in the enteric nervous system (ENS)
claims.quote: We hypothesized GI symptoms in CLN3 disease are at least partially due to neurodegeneration in the enteric nervous system (ENS), the master regulator of bowel function.

claims.object_mention: damage to enteric neurons and glia
claims.quote: Our findings demonstrate that CLN3 deficiency profoundly damages enteric neurons and glia in both murine and human CLN3 disease, contributing to GI dysfunction.
Degenerative changes in Cln3Δex7/8 mouse enteric neurons and glia were largely prevented by systemic neonatal delivery of AAV9.hCLN3 gene therapy, preventing bowel distention at disease endstage.
